Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal

S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  06.06.2024 C482 No. 991 of 2024  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.

1. Mr. Bilal Ahmed, learned counsel for the applicants, Mr. G.S. Sandhu, learned Additional Advocate General assisted by Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State and Mr. A.K.
Beniwal, learned counsel for the respondent.
2.
The instant C482 Application has been moved along with the Compounding Application (IA/1/2024) supported with the affidavits of the applicants and respondent No. 2.
The applicants and respondent No. 2 are present in Court and the applicant No. 3 Smt. Rukshana appears through V.C.
All the applicants and respondent No. 2 are identified by their respective counsel through their Aadhaar Cards.
This Court also interacted with each of them.
3. The son of applicant Nos. 1 & 3 married with respondent No. 2 on 14.01.2019 and due to this wedlock, one son was born.

Unfortunately, the son of applicant Nos. 1 & 3 i.e. the husband of respondent No. 2 died by committed suicide on 02.07.2019 and at the time of suicide, the respondent No. 2 was not with her husband and due to some misunderstanding, after the death of her husband, the respondent No. 2 lodged the First Information Report on 21.08.2019, wherein the present applicants have been implicated for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 498A, 504,
506 of IPC, in which after investigation, the charge sheet has been filed.

4. This Court interacts with respondent No. 2 the complainant, who submits that now she has settled the dispute with her in-laws i.e. applicant Nos. 1 & 3, as well as with her Jeth, i.e. applicant No. 2, she does not want to pursue this proceeding, she lodged the impugned FIR merely on suspicious since at the time of committing suicide by her husband, she was not in the house of her in-laws.
5. This Court, also interact with applicant No. 1 and applicant No. 3 and they submit that they will take all care of respondent No. 2 and her son.
They also undertake before this Court that they will treat the respondent No. 2 as their daughter.

C482/991/2024 on 6 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39762056/
1 6.

Mr. G.S. Sandhu, learned Additional Advocate General for the State fairly submits that after investigation, the charge sheet was filed for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 498-A, 504 and 506 of IPC.

He submits that except the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC, rest of the offenses are compoundable and since the applicants and respondent No. 2 have settled their dispute the offence punishable under Section 498A can be compounded.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and after taking into consideration all these aspects and particularly, keeping in view the fact that husband of respondent No. 2 is no more and the applicants and respondent No. 2 have settled their dispute, this Court is of the view that the compounding application deserves to be allowed.
8. In view of this, the Compounding Application is allowed.

9. Entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 11 of 2023 (State Vs. Rukshana and others) for the offence punishable under Section 323, 498A, 504, 506 of IPC, arising out of FIR No. 0539 of 2019,
Police Station - Laksar, District - Haridwar, pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Laksar, District Haridwar are hereby quashed.
